blocks.text: A PlayStation 1 emulator built for handheld play

EmuCoreR is an Android emulator and game library for the original PlayStation, built around the SwanStation libretro core. It is designed as a complete handheld experience rather than a thin core wrapper: library management, per-game profiles, touch and gamepad controls, save management and an in-game menu all stay usable on a phone screen, a tablet or a television.
The core runs inside a native libretro frontend

The application drives SwanStation through its own JNI libretro frontend. The core's ARM64 recompiler translates guest CPU code with an interpreter fallback, while the frontend negotiates the graphics context and owns audio output, input state, save states and the presentation surface. Keeping that boundary explicit lets the emulator stay close to upstream core behaviour while the Android layer decides how frames are paced and presented.

Rendering can run on Vulkan, OpenGL ES or the software renderer, with internal resolution scaling up to 10x, texture filtering modes such as Nearest, Bilinear, JINC2 and xBR, true colour output, scaled dithering, deinterlacing and NTSC or PAL timing controls. PGXP geometry correction, widescreen hacks, fast boot and software readbacks cover games that depend on precise GPU behaviour.
Controls and sessions designed for the commute

Touch controls live in a layout editor where buttons, sticks and custom controls can be moved, resized and saved as separate profiles. Physical gamepads are mapped per pad and support dead zones, stick sensitivity, rumble forwarding and quick save or quick load shortcuts, while gyroscope input is available for titles that can use it.

Interruptions are expected on a handheld. Quick save and quick load, automatic saves, optional auto-load, visual save previews and a memory card manager keep progress intact when a session is cut short.
Disc images, texture packs, cheats and achievements
The emulator reads CUE/BIN, ISO, IMG, CHD, PBP, ECM, MDS and PSF images, plus M3U playlists for multi-disc games. The library scans folders, matches cover art and keeps recent titles within reach.

Online catalogs integrated into the app bring HD texture packs and cheat sets for supported games. RetroAchievements support tracks official achievement sets, shows per-game progress and raises unlock notifications during play, with both hardcore and softcore scoring and offline progress handling.

The interface is written in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose and is translated into 18 languages. Themes, side artwork, a performance overlay and per-game settings profiles let each title keep its own graphics, control and audio configuration. Disc swapping, renderer switching and quick actions are available from the in-game menu without leaving the session.
Where to find builds and follow development

Builds and localized notes are published on the EmuCoreR website, and the in-app Updates screen links to the same catalog. The Android application itself is closed source, while the SwanStation-derived core and the JNI frontend are published in the project's GitHub repository. BIOS files and game images are not included anywhere.
EmuCoreR does not provide BIOS files or game images. Use your own legally obtained PlayStation BIOS and disc dumps.

Development continues in public commits. Recent work covers catalog synchronisation, cheat management, side artwork alignment, low-latency audio and controller rumble, and compatibility feedback from real devices continues to shape the roadmap.
